name: WAFT
paper_title: WAFT: Warping-Alone Field Transforms for Optical Flow
license: BSD-3-Clause (s, m and l checkpoints); DINOv3 License (t checkpoint)
license_interpretation: The license depends on the size, because each checkpoint embeds a different encoder. The s, m and l checkpoints are BSD-3-Clause, a permissive license that allows commercial and closed-source use as long as the copyright notice, conditions and disclaimer are kept on redistribution; their encoders are Apache-2.0 (Depth Anything V2 Small for s and m, Twins-SVT-Large from timm for l), which is also permissive. The t checkpoint contains a DINOv3 ViT-S/16 fine-tuned by the WAFT authors, so Meta's DINOv3 License applies to it: a custom license, not OSI-approved, with its own use restrictions and conditions; read it before relying on t commercially. Upstream publishes no separate weight license, so LibreYOLO hosts the checkpoints under the repository's BSD-3-Clause license plus the encoder license. The code from princeton-vl/WAFT at commit b152ff1 is vendored under libreyolo/models/waft/_vendor/ (BSD-3-Clause); the encoders reuse code already in LibreYOLO (Depth Anything V2, Apache-2.0; DINOv3 from the DEIMv2 vendor, DINOv3 License) and a plain-torch Twins copy derived from timm (Apache-2.0). LibreYOLO's wrapper code is MIT. Weights come from the upstream Google Drive model zoo and are mirrored on the LibreYOLO Hugging Face org without gating. Inference only.
